`fastapi/encoders.py` is the only file I confirmed implements this. The `jsonable_encoder` function there walks the value recursively. It maps `datetime`, `date` and `time` to ISO strings, `Decimal` to int or float, `Enum` to its `.value`, `UUID` to `str`, and `PurePath` to a string. I did not open the other files that matched my search (`routing.py`, `openapi/utils.py`, `_compat/v2.py` and others), so I can't say whether they call it.

`fastapi/encoders.py`

The `ENCODERS_BY_TYPE` table at line 68 and the `jsonable_encoder` function at line 112 do the conversion, with each type handled by an `isinstance` branch or a table lookup, recursing into dicts, lists and sets.

`fastapi/encoders.py`
`fastapi/routing.py`
`fastapi/_compat/v2.py`

`jsonable_encoder` in `fastapi/encoders.py` does the conversion. It recurses through dicts, lists and tuples, and maps datetimes to ISO strings, Enums to `.value`, Decimals to int or float, and UUIDs to `str`, with Pydantic models dumped in `mode="json"` first. `fastapi/routing.py` calls it on return values before the JSON response is built (around line 317). `fastapi/_compat/v2.py` is the Pydantic v2 compatibility layer that the model-dumping path depends on, but I only grepped it and did not read the serialization code, so it is the least certain of the three.

`fastapi/encoders.py`

The `jsonable_encoder` function recurses through dicts, lists and other containers, and maps each leaf through `ENCODERS_BY_TYPE` (datetimes to ISO strings, `Decimal` to int or float, `Enum` to `.value`, `UUID` to `str`) or the class-based encoders, so the result contains only plain JSON-compatible values.

`fastapi/encoders.py`
`fastapi/routing.py`

`encoders.py` holds `jsonable_encoder` and the `ENCODERS_BY_TYPE` table that maps datetime/date/time, Decimal, Enum, UUID and timedelta to plain values, recursing into nested dicts and lists. `routing.py` calls it from `serialize_response` (around line 317) to convert whatever an endpoint returns before the response is rendered.
